meta.method: Live: Trenitalia lefrecce.it BFF API (ticket/solutions, adults=5); Italo public website biglietti.italotreno.com via Playwright/msedge (captured api-biglietti booking/status JSON, prices in EUR); ÖBB anonymous shop API shop.oebbtickets.at (init / hafas stations / hafas v4 timetable / offer v1 prices, 5 adults). Blocked/unavailable: int.bahn.de (Akamai 403 OPS_BLOCKED), MÁV jegy-a.mav.hu API (connection closed), ÖBB website (Cloudflare bot check; not bypassed). No bookings, no accounts, no personal data.
meta.key_finding: Italy domestic (Roma-Verona, 26 Feb 2027) is ON SALE now at both Trenitalia and Italo. Every Austria/cross-border leg (Verona-Innsbruck, Innsbruck-Wien, Wien-Budapest) is NOT on sale yet: ÖBB and Trenitalia systems only carry the 2026 timetable up to Sat 12 Dec 2026 (probed: 12 Dec returns trains, 13 Dec onwards returns nothing except Nightjets). The 2027 timetable starts Sun 13 Dec 2026. ÖBB's normal horizon is 180 days, so the only thing blocking sales is the loading of the 2027 timetable.
meta.reference_data_note: For the not-yet-open legs, times and prices come from the SAME trains on an equivalent weekday in the current timetable (Sun 29 Nov, Mon 30 Nov, Thu 3 Dec 2026), fetched live on 2026-09-30. They are labelled 'reference, not a live quote for 2027'. Times of the 2027 timetable can shift by a few minutes, and prices can change.

legs.recommendation: Italo 8956, dep 08:20 -> arr 11:38, direct, fare Italo Friends in Smart: EUR 159.80 for all 5 (EUR 31.96 each, about BRL 951 in total). It is the cheapest option in the window, gets you to Verona before noon, and can still be changed for a fee up to 72 h before departure. That is more flexible than Trenitalia's Super Economy (EUR 199.50, no change at all). Put all 5 on ONE booking, because the fare only applies to groups of 3-5. If you want free changes, Italo Flex costs EUR 399.50. The Trenitalia FR 8506 at 08:50 is the backup if Italo sells out. Buy now: prices only go up closer to the date.
legs.notes: Both trains leave from Roma Termini and arrive at Verona Porta Nuova. You don't validate Italo/Frecce e-tickets (they are tied to the train and seat); keep the PDF/QR and ID. Carry-on is fine on both; there are luggage racks at the car ends and overhead. Italo returned fareTypes='foreignFares' and its site showed USD because the search came from Brazil. The JSON prices are in EUR. Pay in EUR on italotreno.com (it/en site) to avoid DCC conversion. Italo Friends seats go fast (81 left at check time).

legs.recommendation: RJ 88, dep 09:01 -> arr 12:32 (reference timetable), direct, fare Sparschiene. Expect about EUR 90-160 for 5 (BRL 535-950) if you buy in the first days of sales. Check 1st class as well, because it was cheaper than 2nd on the reference date. If you want a way out, Trenitalia's Semi Flex (refundable until the day before) often costs little more. Add seat reservations (about EUR 3-3.50 each via ÖBB): Sunday Brenner trains get full. Check the 2027 times when sales open; the 09:01 departure could move a few minutes.
legs.notes: It leaves from Verona Porta Nuova and arrives at Innsbruck Hbf. Since Dec 2025 the EuroCity DB-ÖBB service on this line runs as Railjet (RJ). The ÖBB API returns the RJ 11:01 at EUR 111.60 for 5, more than Trenitalia (EUR 89.50). Nothing to validate on this train (the e-ticket is tied to the train). The Innsbruck Hbf station is central.

legs.recommendation: RJX around 13:58 -> 18:32 (reference RJX 165), direct, fare Sparschiene. On the reference date it was the cheapest in the window at EUR 124.50 for 5 (EUR 24.90 each, about BRL 741), and it leaves the whole morning free in Innsbruck. If you prefer to arrive earlier, take the 12:56 -> 17:32 (EUR 199.50 for 5 on the reference date). Add seat reservations for 5 (about EUR 15-17.50 in total). A Monday midday train is manageable without them, but they make sure the group sits together. Buy on the first days of sales; Sparschiene prices go up in steps as seats sell.
legs.notes: It leaves from Innsbruck Hbf and arrives at Wien Hbf. No departure between 11:00 and 12:42 on the reference date (the 10:56 RJX is just before the window). The 12:42 RJ 88 via Germany (753.50 for 5) should be avoided. WESTbahn: no WESTbahn departures from Innsbruck appeared in the ÖBB timetable data, and WESTbahn cannot be booked through ÖBB. As far as I know it runs Wien-Salzburg only, so you would need a change in Salzburg for no gain. Not checked live. Nothing to validate; show the QR plus ID.

legs.recommendation: Go out on the 07:40 RJX (arr 10:35) and come back on the 16:30 EC 148 (back in Wien 19:20), both on Sparschiene. Expect about EUR 155 for 5 in total (about BRL 923). That gives about 6 h in Budapest with a comfortable evening arrival. If you want the latest train that still arrives by 20:20, take the 17:30. Buy both tickets together on the opening days. Sparschiene is train-bound, so a missed return means buying a new ticket. Anyone who wants a buffer should take the standard fare only for the return.
legs.notes: Departure and return are at Budapest-Keleti. The return leg is the cheap one (EUR 14.90 each on the reference date).
